items.headline: Tech sell-off hits Friday: Nasdaq falls about 2.8%, S&P 500 about 1.8%, Dow about 1.1%
items.note: The Dow closed at 51,770.31. Amazon and Alphabet earnings misses and Intel's weak outlook renewed worries about Big Tech's AI spending. For October, the Nasdaq fell roughly 5%, the S&P 500 about 1.2%, and the Dow gained about 1.5%. Figures vary a little by source.

items.headline: Two Fed officials hint rate hikes may be needed; oil rises on Middle East tensions
items.note: Both added to Friday's pressure on stocks, per the market recap. Higher rates tend to hit richly valued tech shares hardest.

items.headline: Amazon's free cash flow turns to a $42.4B outflow as it holds 2026 capex at $220B
items.note: Amazon fell about 4% on Thursday after reporting and was part of Friday's tech sell-off. Heavy AI spending is now the main thing investors question.

items.headline: Alphabet's record one-day drop (about 12% Thursday) revives worries about when AI spending pays off
items.note: Third-quarter sales missed estimates and about $500 billion in value was erased. Big Tech's AI budgets set how much these firms hire for ML roles.

items.headline: Intel plunges roughly 17-20% on a weak revenue outlook
items.note: Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15-16B versus about $17B expected. Chip stocks are priced on forward guidance, not just past results.

items.headline: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic agree to honor one robots.txt token for opting out of AI training
items.note: Websites can use `__usage_ai-training` to opt out across all four companies' crawlers. Anthropic has started; OpenAI says coming months, Microsoft targets Feb 1, 2027, Google 2027. It is an individual IETF draft with no formal standing, and non-compliant scrapers can ignore it.

items.headline: Economy grew at a 3.4% pace in Q3, but inflation is still running hot
items.note: Initial GDP beat the 3.1% expected. September PCE inflation rose 3.6% from a year earlier (core 3.1%). Strong growth plus high inflation keeps Fed hikes in play, per reports.

items.headline: Entry-level tech postings are scarce, though data roles look steadier than most
items.note: A report covered by Careers360 on Oct. 27 found only 4.3% of live tech postings (India-focused data) were entry or junior level, and data engineering's share nearly doubled. Recruiting blogs say US data scientist listings have grown while overall tech listings sit below their pre-pandemic peak; those are vendor sources, so treat them as indicative.

learn.explain: A correction is when a stock or index falls roughly 10% from a recent high. It is milder than a bear market, which is usually a drop of 20% or more. Corrections are common and often follow a period when prices rose faster than earnings. This month the Nasdaq fell about 5% as investors questioned whether huge AI spending will pay off. That is a rough month, but not a correction by this definition.
